items.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
items.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about 63 million square miles, larger than all land area combined.

items.question: Which country has the most natural lakes?
items.explanation: Canada has over 3 million lakes, more than the rest of the world combined.

items.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
items.explanation: Vatican City is only 0.17 square miles and is located within Rome, Italy.

items.question: Which river is the longest in the world?
items.explanation: The Nile stretches about 6,650 km through northeastern Africa.

items.question: Mount Everest is located in which mountain range?
items.explanation: Mount Everest is in the Himalayas, on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

items.question: What is the capital of France?
items.explanation: Paris has been the capital since 987 CE and is known as the City of Light.

items.question: Which desert is the largest in the world?
items.explanation: The Antarctic Desert is the largest, covering about 5.5 million square miles.

items.question: What is the deepest point in the ocean?
items.explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench reaches about 36,000 feet below sea level.

items.question: Which African country has the most pyramids?
items.explanation: Sudan has over 200 pyramids, more than Egypt's approximately 100.

items.question: What is the largest island in the world?
items.explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island, covering about 836,000 square miles.

items.question: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
items.explanation: Japan is called Nippon or Nihon, meaning 'origin of the sun' in Japanese.

items.question: What is the capital of Canada?
items.explanation: Ottawa became the capital in 1857, chosen by Queen Victoria.

items.question: Which U.S. state is the largest by area?
items.explanation: Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas, the second-largest state.

items.question: The Great Barrier Reef is off the coast of which country?
items.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches over 1,400 miles along Australia's northeast coast.

items.question: What is the longest river in Europe?
items.explanation: The Volga River in Russia flows about 2,300 miles.

items.question: Which country has the most time zones?
items.explanation: France has 12 time zones due to its overseas territories worldwide.

items.question: What is the highest waterfall in the world?
items.explanation: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops about 3,212 feet.

items.question: Which continent has the most countries?
items.explanation: Africa has 54 recognized countries, the most of any continent.

items.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
items.explanation: Brasília was purpose-built and became the capital in 1960.

items.question: Which sea is the saltiest on Earth?
items.explanation: The Dead Sea has a salinity of about 34%, making it nearly 10 times saltier than the ocean.

items.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
items.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum' meaning gold.

items.question: What planet is known as the Red Planet?
items.explanation: Mars appears red due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

items.question: What is the speed of light?
items.explanation: Light travels at approximately 299,792 km/s in a vacuum.

items.question: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
items.explanation: Diamond rates 10 on the Mohs hardness scale, the highest possible rating.

items.question: Which gas do plants absorb from the atmosphere?
items.explanation: Plants use CO2 during photosynthesis to produce glucose and oxygen.

items.question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
items.explanation: The skin covers about 22 square feet and makes up roughly 16% of body weight.

items.question: What particle has a negative charge?
items.explanation: Electrons carry a negative charge and orbit the nucleus of an atom.

items.question: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
items.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

items.question: Which blood type is the universal donor?
items.explanation: O-negative can be donated to any blood type because it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens.

items.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
items.explanation: Mitochondria produce ATP, the cell's main energy currency.

items.question: How many elements are in the periodic table?
items.explanation: As of 2024, there are 118 confirmed elements in the periodic table.

items.question: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
items.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (212°F) at standard atmospheric pressure.

items.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
items.explanation: Mercury orbits the Sun at an average distance of about 36 million miles.

items.question: What is the study of fossils called?
items.explanation: Paleontologists study fossils to understand ancient life and Earth's history.

items.question: Which vitamin is produced when skin is exposed to sunlight?
items.explanation: UVB rays trigger vitamin D synthesis in the skin.

items.question: What is the main gas found in the Sun?
items.explanation: The Sun is about 73% hydrogen and 25% helium by mass.

items.question: What is the smallest unit of life?
items.explanation: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

items.question: Which animal has the largest brain?
items.explanation: A blue whale's brain can weigh up to 15 pounds, the heaviest of any animal.

items.question: What does DNA stand for?
items.explanation: DNA contains the genetic instructions for the development and function of living things.

items.question: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
items.explanation: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at standard room temperature and pressure.

items.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
items.explanation: Jupiter is so large that over 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

items.question: How many teeth does an adult human have?
items.explanation: Adults typically have 32 teeth, including wisdom teeth.

items.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
items.explanation: Water consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

items.question: Which organ filters blood in the human body?
items.explanation: The kidneys filter about 120-150 quarts of blood daily to produce urine.

items.question: What causes the Earth's seasons?
items.explanation: Earth's 23.5-degree axial tilt causes different parts to receive more sunlight throughout the year.

items.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
items.explanation: George Washington served as the first U.S. President from 1789 to 1797.

items.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
items.explanation: The RMS Titanic sank on April 15, 1912, after hitting an iceberg.

items.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
items.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa between 1503 and 1519.

items.question: Which empire was ruled by Genghis Khan?
items.explanation: Genghis Khan united Mongol tribes and created the largest contiguous land empire in history.

items.question: When did the Berlin Wall fall?
items.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989, symbolizing the end of the Cold War.

items.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
items.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on July 20, 1969, saying 'That's one small step for man...'

items.question: Which ancient wonder of the world still stands today?
items.explanation: The Great Pyramid of Giza was completed around 2560 BCE and remains largely intact.

items.question: Who wrote the play 'Romeo and Juliet'?
items.explanation: Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet around 1594-1596.

items.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
items.explanation: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on July 14.

items.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
items.explanation: The Inca Empire built Machu Picchu in the 15th century in modern-day Peru.

items.question: Who invented the telephone?
items.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell was awarded the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876.

items.question: What was the name of the ship on which Charles Darwin sailed?
items.explanation: Darwin sailed on HMS Beagle from 1831 to 1836, leading to his theory of evolution.

items.question: Which U.S. state was the last to join the Union?
items.explanation: Hawaii became the 50th U.S. state on August 21, 1959.

items.question: Who was the longest-reigning British monarch?
items.explanation: Queen Elizabeth II reigned for over 70 years from 1952 to 2022.

items.question: The Renaissance began in which country?
items.explanation: The Renaissance began in Florence, Italy, in the 14th century.

items.question: Who discovered penicillin?
items.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from mold growing in a petri dish.

items.question: Which war was fought between the North and South in the United States?
items.explanation: The American Civil War was fought from 1861 to 1865.

items.question: Who was the first Emperor of Rome?
items.explanation: Augustus, born Octavian, became the first Roman Emperor in 27 BCE.

items.question: In which year did the Internet become publicly available?
items.explanation: The World Wide Web became publicly available in 1993, though the Internet existed earlier.

items.question: Which ancient civilization invented paper?
items.explanation: Paper was invented in China during the Han Dynasty around 105 CE by Cai Lun.

items.question: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
items.explanation: The five rings represent the five inhabited continents of the world.

items.question: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
items.explanation: Uruguay won the first World Cup, defeating Argentina 4-2 in the final.

items.question: In tennis, what is the term for a score of zero?
items.explanation: The term 'love' comes from the French word 'l'oeuf' meaning egg, symbolizing zero.

items.question: Which NBA team has won the most championships?
items.explanation: The Boston Celtics have won 17 NBA championships, tied with the Lakers.

items.question: What is the length of a marathon?
items.explanation: A marathon is exactly 26 miles and 385 yards (42.195 kilometers).

items.question: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
items.explanation: Badminton uses a shuttlecock, also called a birdie.

items.question: How many periods are in a standard ice hockey game?
items.explanation: A standard ice hockey game has three 20-minute periods.

items.question: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
items.explanation: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens, Greece.

items.question: What is the highest score possible in a single frame of bowling?
items.explanation: A perfect frame with two strikes in the tenth frame can score 30 points.

items.question: In cricket, how many balls are in an over?
items.explanation: An over in cricket consists of six legal deliveries bowled by one bowler.

items.question: Which golfer has won the most major championships?
items.explanation: Jack Nicklaus won 18 major championships during his career.

items.question: What color is the jersey worn by the leader of the Tour de France?
items.explanation: The yellow jersey (maillot jaune) signifies the overall race leader.

items.question: Which sport is known as 'the beautiful game'?
items.explanation: Soccer (football) is widely known as 'the beautiful game', coined by Pelé.

items.question: How many players are on a baseball team on the field?
items.explanation: A baseball team fields 9 players at a time.

items.question: Which boxer was known as 'The Greatest'?
items.explanation: Muhammad Ali called himself 'The Greatest' and is widely considered one of the best ever.

items.question: In which sport would you perform a slam dunk?
items.explanation: A slam dunk is when a player forces the ball through the hoop from above.

items.question: Which country won the most gold medals at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
items.explanation: The United States topped the medal table at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

items.question: How many Grand Slam tennis tournaments are there?
items.explanation: The four Grand Slams are Wimbledon, US Open, French Open, and Australian Open.

items.question: What is the national sport of Japan?
items.explanation: Sumo wrestling is considered Japan's national sport.

items.question: Which NFL team has won the most Super Bowls?
items.explanation: The Pittsburgh Steelers have won 6 Super Bowls, tied with the Patriots.

items.explanation: The median is the middle number when arranged in order: 9.

items.explanation: An epiphany is a moment of sudden revelation or insight.

items.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly, wishing to do good.

items.explanation: Ambiguous means having more than one possible meaning or interpretation.

items.question: What does 'meticulous' mean?
items.explanation: A meticulous person is very careful and precise in their work.

items.question: What does 'nostalgia' mean?

items.question: What does 'resilient' mean?
items.explanation: Resilient means able to withstand or recover quickly from difficulties.

items.question: What does 'eloquent' mean?

items.question: What does 'pragmatic' mean?

items.question: What does 'candid' mean?
